docs/decisions/058-get-relevant-context-topic-search-search-records-bm25-over-l.md:3:Commit caa6e387e6 (Merge search-records-integration). src/graph/mod.rs relevant_context(): entity_index.search_classes(t, &class_iris, &state.store, &data_graphs, moose::LABEL_PREDICATES, limit) replaced by entity_index.search_records(t, &class_iris, &state.store, &data_graphs, &text_fields, limit). text_fields = [(moose::RDFS_LABEL, 2.0_f32), (state.capture.description.as_str(), 1.0_f32)] — rdfs:label weighted 2× because every record carries it as its title; description weighted 1×. Tool remains purely symbolic: no LLM on the retrieval path.

docs/decisions/003-alignment-index-built-at-startup-via-appstate-build-alignmen.md:3:Commit fbe9777ed8 (M2 fixes, src/graph/mod.rs, src/main.rs). AppState::build_alignment_index() is a separate async method (not part of bootstrap) called at startup in main.rs. Separation from bootstrap keeps non-aligning code paths (e.g., M1 capture/query tests) free from the embedding-backbone load. Non-fatal by design: if the embedding model can't load (offline with no bundled weights), a tracing::warn is emitted but the server continues — only align_concepts/suggest_mappings are disabled; capture, query, context, and provenance tools are unaffected. The built VecStore is stored on AppState.vector_store (Arc) and also wired into engine_config.embedding_store, which additionally sharpens query-time class disambiguation beyond its primary alignment role. Rationale for startup build vs. precompute script: simpler deployment (no separate CLI step); fresh-rebuild each start keeps the index coherent with the loaded ontologies.

docs/decisions/024-kg-iri-conventions-named-graph-kg-project-instances-at-kg-cl.md:3:Commit 64f9fbf1b7 (src/graph/mod.rs: PROJECT_KG_GRAPH_IRI, mint_instance_iri). Two stable IRI conventions established: (1) all recorded knowledge instances live in the named graph https://moosedev.dev/kg/project — this is the data graph passed to execute_graph_walk_nlq_with_context and targeted by SPARQL queries; (2) instance IRIs are minted as https://moosedev.dev/kg/{class_local}/{uuid4}, e.g. https://moosedev.dev/kg/ArchitecturalDecision/<uuid>. Rationale: predictable, collision-free IRIs; class name in the IRI aids human readability and allows SPARQL queries to filter by path prefix; the named graph isolates project knowledge from the ontology/vocabulary graphs loaded into the same Store.

./docs/decisions/016-bootstrap-must-produce-typed-edges-so-relational-expansion-r.md:1:# Bootstrap must produce typed edges so relational expansion reaches lexically-distant context
./docs/decisions/016-bootstrap-must-produce-typed-edges-so-relational-expansion-r.md:3:skills/bootstrap-existing-codebase.md (commit 9114ee7a73, intro rewrite): "only a linked graph lets you follow 'why?' from a decision to rationale that lives in a lexically-distant record. Flat keyword retrieval finds a single record; only a linked graph lets you follow." The bootstrap workflow exists partly to seed the graph for get_relevant_context relational expansion — but expansion only reaches linked neighbors; if bootstrap produces only isolated nodes, the expansion step is useless. Therefore the bootstrap must write typed edges, not just typed nodes.

docs/decisions/046-recall-first-means-list-all-a-topic-scoped-empty-result-is-n.md:3:Commit 2145d71c95 (tasks/lessons.md). During the M4 bootstrap-skill dry-run, `get_relevant_context` was called with a specific topic, returned "No recorded knowledge relevant to …", and the agent concluded the graph was empty — then recorded decisions that already existed, creating duplicates. Rule: the recall-first step must be a list-all call (`get_relevant_context` with no `topic` parameter). A topic-scoped call returns only records whose embeddings align to that topic; it can silently miss related records that were captured under different framing. List-all is the only safe dedup check before recording. Apply at the start of every capture session and every temporal-bootstrap episode.

./docs/decisions/022-don-t-index-instance-data-for-a-box-recall-moose-walk-planni.md:3:Commit 17bcfda8 / tasks/lessons.md addition. Pattern surfaced during investigation of `get_relevant_context` imprecision: the temptation was to improve recall quality via embedding-ranked A-box recall or embedding-based instance dedup — building a vector index over recorded instance content. This contradicts a deliberate MOOSE design choice: MOOSE deliberately does NOT index instance data; walk planning was devised to avoid the vector-index/RAG trap and deliver more precise, auditable retrieval.
./docs/decisions/022-don-t-index-instance-data-for-a-box-recall-moose-walk-planni.md:5:Rule: when recall, dedup, or contradiction detection seems to need "semantic search" over recorded instances, reach for the symbolic path first — `query` (walk planning) and `sparql` for retrieval precision; LLM-as-sensor + typed conflict for contradiction — not a nearest-neighbor index over instances. Embeddings in MOOSEDev are confined to T-box term alignment (`suggest_parent`) over the static ontology (class placement, not instance retrieval). `get_relevant_context` is a shallow lexical anchor/browse tool by construction; fix its imprecision with an honesty floor + tool-selection guidance, not vector search.
./docs/decisions/026-lesson-export-corpus-py-must-query-rdfs-label-not-hastitle-t.md:3:Commit 29cac60c28 (`bench/export_corpus.py`). The prior SPARQL query joined on `?s a ?kind ; ?tp ?title . FILTER(STRENDS(STR(?tp), "hasTitle"))`, which required a `hasTitle` triple. SystemComponent records carry `hasComponentName` as their typed label property (not `hasTitle`) and have no `hasTitle` triple — so they were silently excluded from the B1 corpus export, creating a hidden parity violation: B1 was missing a class of records that B2 could retrieve.
./docs/decisions/026-lesson-export-corpus-py-must-query-rdfs-label-not-hastitle-t.md:5:Fix: query on `<http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#label>` directly — the canonical label MOOSE writes for every captured record, across all kinds. This mirrors the B2 retrieval-side switch to rdfs:label (search_records text fields). Rule: the SPARQL export must anchor on rdfs:label for enumeration; type-specific title predicates (hasTitle, hasComponentName) vary by class and cause silent gaps. The decouple-code-from-ontology discipline applies to the export side as much as the retrieval side.

Replaced by text_fields = [(RDFS_LABEL, 2.0), (state.capture.description, 1.0)] passed to entity_index.search_records(). BM25 scores are corpus-relative — results ranked top-k, no absolute threshold. Records sharing no query term are excluded by search_records itself, preserving invariant #6 (be correct, don't sound correct) without a fragile constant. tests/context.rs: noise-rejection test updated from "transport tuning methodology" (single incidental token overlap) to "kubernetes helm rollout" (genuinely zero shared terms), verifying BM25 exclusion rather than the old score floor. docs/decisions/060-get-relevant-context-bounded-relational-expansion-follows-re.md:1:# get_relevant_context: bounded relational expansion follows record→record edges from BM25 seeds
docs/decisions/060-get-relevant-context-bounded-relational-expansion-follows-re.md:3:Commit 5dc4a3ba00 (src/graph/mod.rs relevant_context() + record_neighbors()). After BM25 retrieval produces a ranked seed set, get_relevant_context performs a bounded hop-walk over outbound record→record edges (record_neighbors()) to surface lexically-distant records that are linked to the seeds but would be missed by pure keyword matching. Implementation details:
docs/decisions/060-get-relevant-context-bounded-relational-expansion-follows-re.md:5:- record_neighbors(iri): enumerates all outbound quads from a project-graph subject in the project KG graph. Skips rdf:type, prov: metadata firehose, and hasRationale (its text is already inlined by build_context_item). Returns (predicate_local, neighbor_iri, neighbor_class) for neighbors that pass require_information_record — only recorded knowledge items, not arbitrary graph nodes.
docs/decisions/060-get-relevant-context-bounded-relational-expansion-follows-re.md:11:Rationale: BM25 ranks by shared tokens — a Constraint whose title shares no tokens with the query but is linked via isMotivatedBy from a matching ArchitecturalDecision is invisible to BM25 alone. Traversal reaches it in one hop. The bounded budget (Constraint f28b0186) ensures this does not become a neighborhood dump that defeats context efficiency. The symbolic-layer principle is preserved: no LLM involvement on the expansion path.
docs/decisions/011-benchmark-grading-anti-circularity-ground-truth-is-the-sourc.md:3:Commit 7633402925 (`bench/grade.py`, `bench/grade_code.py`, `bench/bootstrap_rust_rfcs.py`). A fundamental grading principle: the benchmark's ground truth is the **original source corpus** (the codebase, RFC texts, etc.) — never the in-graph records. This prevents circularity: if the in-graph records were themselves used to define ground truth, B2 would be scored against the very content it retrieves, trivially winning.
./docs/decisions/065-query-adds-puresymbolic-fallback-when-schemaqueryspec-intern.md:3:Commit 69f8f01389 (src/graph/mod.rs, tests/query.rs). `query()` is refactored into three layers: private `execute_query()` takes explicit `llm` + `engine_config` refs; public `query()` calls `execute_query` with the state's own llm/model/engine_config; `#[doc(hidden)]` pub `query_with_llm_client()` accepts an injected `&dyn LlmClient` for test determinism. The fallback logic lives in `query_with_llm_client`: if the assist level is not PureSymbolic and the returned answer contains the internal sentinel string `SCHEMA_QUERY_SPEC_INTERNAL_ERROR` ("Schema query intent set but no SchemaQuerySpec was attached"), the pipeline retries with `llm_assist_level = LlmAssistLevel::PureSymbolic` on a cloned config. Rationale: `execute_graph_walk_nlq_with_context` can emit that sentinel as a diagnostic when a schema-query intent is resolved but no SchemaQuerySpec is attached, and without the fallback that internal error leaks verbatim to the MCP caller. The regression test `query_does_not_surface_schema_spec_internal_error_for_project_records` uses `MetaIntentLlm` (a stub that returns a meta-intent JSON response) to trigger the code path and assert that (a) the error string never reaches the answer, and (b) the trace confirms PureSymbolic was used on the retry.

docs/decisions/009-benchmark-content-parity-b1-export-carries-exactly-the-recor.md:5:Implementation: `export_corpus.py` pulls every record from the project graph via a deterministic SPARQL SELECT over `kg/project` (predicates matched by local-name via STRENDS, per the decouple-code-from-ontology-ttl lesson). docs/decisions/074-supersede-decision-atomic-lifecycle-new-decision-rationale-n.md:3:Commit e7c7f07dae (src/graph/mod.rs, spec/supersede-and-relations.md). `supersede_decision(state, input: &SupersedeInput, author, when)` is a new domain function and MCP tool (kept separate from `record_important_decision`, whose contract is "record a fresh item"). Key design decisions: (1) Atomicity — new decision, Rationale node, `supersedes`/`hasRationale` edges, and old decision's `hasLifecycleStatus` flip to "superseded" all commit in one transaction; entity index invalidated once on success. (2) The old record is NEVER deleted — it is preserved as history with status "superseded"; "what we used to think, what we think now, and why" becomes a walkable subgraph. (3) Rationale is a first-class `Rationale` node (not a plain string) — the why is independently queryable and linkable (invariant #2). (4) Precondition: `superseded_iri` must exist in the project graph and be an ArchitecturalDecision (or subclass); errors + writes nothing if violated. (5) The spec (spec/supersede-and-relations.md) describes three phases: Phase 1 (object-property plumbing) and Phase 2 (supersede_decision) are implemented in this commit; Phase 3 (lifecycle-aware read path — exclude superseded from default get_relevant_context) is outstanding.

docs/decisions/034-memory-must-be-external-and-queryable-not-stuffed-into-conte.md:1:# Memory must be external and queryable, not stuffed into context window
docs/decisions/034-memory-must-be-external-and-queryable-not-stuffed-into-conte.md:3:Design Invariant #5 from CLAUDE.md (initial commit 455628e081). Do not rely on stuffing large amounts of history or context into the LLM's context window. Use MOOSEDev's session/project knowledge graph as the primary long-term memory. Rationale: reducing dependence on ever-growing context windows is a core project goal; the knowledge graph must be the authoritative store.

docs/decisions/002-agent-recall-first-protocol-for-self-hosted-mcp-get-relevant.md:1:# Agent recall-first protocol for self-hosted MCP: get_relevant_context → short NLQ → record → align_concepts → validate
docs/decisions/002-agent-recall-first-protocol-for-self-hosted-mcp-get-relevant.md:3:Commit 85cd7821cc (CLAUDE.md "Dogfooding MOOSEDev" section). Codifies the operating discipline for agents using the self-hosted MCP: (1) Recall first — get_relevant_context or query before non-trivial work; (2) Keep NLQ questions short — one focused sentence per query call; (3) Capture as you go — record_important_decision with kind ArchitecturalDecision/Lesson/Constraint/Pattern/AntiPattern/Requirement; capture decision + rationale, not transient chatter; (4) Align new concepts with align_concepts before introducing a new term to prevent model graph drift (Invariant #4); (5) Verify with validate_against_architecture after capturing; use sparql for precise deterministic reads. Rationale: makes agent use of MOOSEDev reliable and disciplined — recall prevents duplication, alignment prevents drift, validation ensures consistency. Explicitly stated: "When its tools are available, prefer them over re-deriving context (invariant #5)."

docs/decisions/026-lesson-export-corpus-py-must-query-rdfs-label-not-hastitle-t.md:3:Commit 29cac60c28 (`bench/export_corpus.py`). The prior SPARQL query joined on `?s a ?kind ; ?tp ?title . FILTER(STRENDS(STR(?tp), "hasTitle"))`, which required a `hasTitle` triple. SystemComponent records carry `hasComponentName` as their typed label property (not `hasTitle`) and have no `hasTitle` triple — so they were silently excluded from the B1 corpus export, creating a hidden parity violation: B1 was missing a class of records that B2 could retrieve.
docs/decisions/026-lesson-export-corpus-py-must-query-rdfs-label-not-hastitle-t.md:5:Fix: query on `<http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#label>` directly — the canonical label MOOSE writes for every captured record, across all kinds. This mirrors the B2 retrieval-side switch to rdfs:label (search_records text fields). Rule: the SPARQL export must anchor on rdfs:label for enumeration; type-specific title predicates (hasTitle, hasComponentName) vary by class and cause silent gaps. The decouple-code-from-ontology discipline applies to the export side as much as the retrieval side.
docs/decisions/015-bootstrap-instance-dedup-link-or-mint-query-before-minting-r.md:3:skills/bootstrap-existing-codebase.md "Link-or-mint grounding" section (commit 9114ee7a73): "Before creating a node, check whether an equivalent instance already exists: get_relevant_context(topic: '<the node's concept in 3-6 words>') and inspect returns of the same kind. Match: reuse the existing IRI — do not mint. No match: mint and capture the new IRI. Test: 'Would a maintainer say these are the same requirement/constraint, or two different ones?' Bias toward reuse for Requirement/Constraint — they recur across many decisions, and reuse is what creates the hub nodes that make the graph multi-hop. Bias toward mint for Consequence/Alternative — usually specific to one decision."
docs/decisions/043-rationale-get-relevant-context-topic-search-search-records-b.md:1:# Rationale: get_relevant_context topic search: search_records (BM25 over label + description) replaces search_classes (label-only)
docs/decisions/007-benchmark-arm-isolation-identical-compaction-config-across-a.md:3:Commit 29cac60c28 (`bench/run.py` `arm_opencode_config()`). All arms now receive an identical `"compaction": {"auto": true, "prune": true, "reserved": 16384}` block in the per-run `opencode.json`. Rationale: opencode's auto-compaction requires a `reserved` headroom buffer to fire *before* a turn overflows the context window; without it, a read-heavy agent silently hits LM Studio TruncateMiddle (server-side middle-truncation), corrupting the run with no visible signal. `prune` drops old accumulated tool outputs to prevent context balloon. These settings are frozen and identical across all arms — memory is the only independent variable. Context management behavior must not confound the comparison.
docs/decisions/014-bootstrap-edge-anti-confabulation-evidence-or-skip-per-edge-.md:3:skills/bootstrap-existing-codebase.md "Anti-confabulation discipline" section (commit 9114ee7a73): "Edges are not SHACL-required, and get_relevant_context tells agents to TRUST recorded knowledge — so a fabricated edge is a durable false claim. Therefore: Evidence-or-skip, per edge. Cite the doc line / code fact / commit that states the relationship (X drove / violates / resulted-in Y) — not merely that both nodes exist. If you can't point to it, don't draw the edge. Prefer not-linking over guessing. A missing edge is honest comprehension debt; a wrong one is served as truth forever. Under-link rather than over-link. No transitive invention." Evidence for a relationship must be the relationship itself, not mere co-presence of nodes.
docs/decisions/012-benchmark-oracle-mode-harness-side-retrieval-isolates-knowle.md:1:# Benchmark oracle mode: harness-side retrieval isolates knowledge-value from fetch-willingness
docs/decisions/012-benchmark-oracle-mode-harness-side-retrieval-isolates-knowle.md:3:Commit 29cac60c28 (`bench/run.py`). A `mode="oracle"` parameter on `run_cell()` causes the harness to retrieve relevant knowledge and prepend it verbatim to the prompt, without giving the agent a live memory tool. This isolates two confounds: H8 (fetch-willingness — whether the agent chooses to call the memory tool) and knowledge-value (whether the knowledge itself helps). If oracle does not beat B0, the captured knowledge has no value; if live-tool < oracle, the gap is fetch-willingness alone.
docs/decisions/012-benchmark-oracle-mode-harness-side-retrieval-isolates-knowle.md:5:Implementation: `oracle_context()` calls `get_relevant_context` for B2 (current-only, symbolic BM25); `freetext_oracle_context()` runs BM25 over the exported chunk file for B1 arms (currency-blind — superseded chunks are retrievable, same as what a B1-rag agent would get). Topic is `task["memory_topic"] or task["prompt"]` — a focused subject phrase so the retrieval signal is unambiguous.
docs/decisions/012-benchmark-oracle-mode-harness-side-retrieval-isolates-knowle.md:7:Oracle asymmetry is intentional: the B2−B1 oracle delta isolates B2's currency-awareness (the agent acting on lifecycle status) rather than information withholding (B1 oracle would also retrieve superseded chunks, so if B2 oracle correctly ignores a superseded record and B1 oracle uses it, that gap is earned).
./docs/decisions/074-supersede-decision-atomic-lifecycle-new-decision-rationale-n.md:3:Commit e7c7f07dae (src/graph/mod.rs, spec/supersede-and-relations.md). `supersede_decision(state, input: &SupersedeInput, author, when)` is a new domain function and MCP tool (kept separate from `record_important_decision`, whose contract is "record a fresh item"). Key design decisions: (1) Atomicity — new decision, Rationale node, `supersedes`/`hasRationale` edges, and old decision's `hasLifecycleStatus` flip to "superseded" all commit in one transaction; entity index invalidated once on success. (2) The old record is NEVER deleted — it is preserved as history with status "superseded"; "what we used to think, what we think now, and why" becomes a walkable subgraph. (3) Rationale is a first-class `Rationale` node (not a plain string) — the why is independently queryable and linkable (invariant #2). (4) Precondition: `superseded_iri` must exist in the project graph and be an ArchitecturalDecision (or subclass); errors + writes nothing if violated. (5) The spec (spec/supersede-and-relations.md) describes three phases: Phase 1 (object-property plumbing) and Phase 2 (supersede_decision) are implemented in this commit; Phase 3 (lifecycle-aware read path — exclude superseded from default get_relevant_context) is outstanding.
docs/decisions/035-ontology-regeneration-orphans-existing-records-migration-sto.md:3:Commit fbe9777ed8 (M2 fixes, tasks/todo.md "Known limitations" section). Instances in the durable KG carry the full class IRI as rdf:type. If a regenerated ontology changes class IRIs or namespace, prior durable records stop being returned by relevant_context/query because those tools build candidate sets from the current arch_vocab. Zero impact today (no persistent production data), but this becomes a data-loss risk before real data accrues. Required mitigation: a deliberate migration story (re-type instances on ontology change via a mapping — NOT hardcoded old namespaces, which would violate the namespace convention decision). Lighter partial step identified: make list-all enumerate by actual rdf:type in the project graph rather than the current vocab. Classified P1 (must be resolved before real data accrues).
docs/decisions/061-get-relevant-context-pure-symbolic-context-retrieval-via-ent.md:1:# get_relevant_context: pure-symbolic context retrieval via entity index (topic) or list-all (no topic)
docs/decisions/061-get-relevant-context-pure-symbolic-context-retrieval-via-ent.md:3:Commit bddba142 (M1 completion) adds the `get_relevant_context` MCP tool and its supporting graph layer: `relevant_context()`, `list_instances()`, `build_context_item()`, and the public `ContextItem` struct. When a non-empty topic is provided the tool searches via the cache-coherent entity index (`entity_index.search_classes()`); when the topic is omitted or blank it enumerates all instances of the ontology's classes in the project KG graph via SPARQL quad iteration. Explicitly pure-symbolic: no LLM call on the retrieval path (tool description: "Symbolic — no LLM"). Returns structured ContextItem objects (kind, label, literal properties, IRI) formatted as a readable block by `format_context()`. Limit is clamped to 1–100 at the MCP layer. Test: `tests/context.rs` (hermetic, two-decision fixture; both list-all and topic-filtered paths exercised). Completes M1: live tools are `ping`, `record_important_decision`, `query` (+trace), `get_relevant_context`; 5 tests green, clippy clean. Record → restart → read-back across two separate processes (shared data dir) also verified.

docs/decisions/056-context-qa-tasks-materialize-docs-stripped-code-tree-so-cold.md:1:# context_qa tasks materialize docs-stripped code tree so cold agent actively searches and fails
docs/decisions/056-context-qa-tasks-materialize-docs-stripped-code-tree-so-cold.md:3:Commit 29cac60c28 (`bench/run.py`): `TREE_TASK_TYPES = {"constraint_code", "context_qa"}`. Q&A tasks typed `context_qa` now receive a materialized, docs-stripped working tree (same `materialize_tree()` as code tasks) rather than an empty workdir. Rationale: the comprehension-debt premise requires that a cold/memory-less agent actively searches code and *fails to find* stripped rationale — not that the code is simply absent from the workdir. With the code tree present, a cold arm "flails hunting for the stripped rationale"; the memory arm short-circuits that search. Graded on final assistant message text (not a patch diff), so no `git_baseline()` is needed. Tasks may opt out with `"materialize_tree": false` for pure memory-currency Q&A where even the code tree is unnecessary.
docs/decisions/047-relational-expansion-in-get-relevant-context-must-be-bounded.md:1:# Relational expansion in get_relevant_context must be bounded: budgeted reach, not neighborhood dump
docs/decisions/047-relational-expansion-in-get-relevant-context-must-be-bounded.md:3:Commit 5dc4a3ba00 (src/graph/mod.rs, EXPAND_FROM_TOP/EXPAND_MAX_HOPS/EXPAND_MAX constants). Relational expansion in get_relevant_context is a budgeted reach to the few linked records that complete an answer — specifically the lexically-distant neighbor that BM25 alone misses — without dumping the full neighborhood. Concretely: expansion seeds from only the top-N BM25 hits (EXPAND_FROM_TOP=3), walks at most EXPAND_MAX_HOPS=2 hops outward, and appends at most EXPAND_MAX=5 total linked records. Context efficiency is the whole point of get_relevant_context: returning the entire reachable neighborhood would negate the retrieval tool's purpose of surfacing the most relevant records without overwhelming the caller's context window. Expansion is skipped entirely for list-all calls and when MOOSEDEV_EXPAND_HOPS=0.
docs/decisions/076-templates-claude-md-distributable-agent-config-template-enco.md:3:Commit 5d688415ad adds templates/CLAUDE.md — a reusable, drop-in CLAUDE.md template for any project that adopts the MOOSEDev MCP server as long-term memory. The template encodes the full graph-first workflow: (1) recall-first (list-all get_relevant_context before non-trivial work; a topic-scoped empty result is not an empty graph); (2) capture as typed records (record_important_decision with appropriate kind, including rationale and rejected alternatives; always report what was written); (3) align before coining new terms (align_concepts / suggest_mappings); (4) correct via supersede_decision or retract_decision — never silently duplicate; (5) validate with validate_against_architecture after capturing. Includes a tool-selection ladder (get_relevant_context → query → sparql, cheap → precise), a capture-kinds cheat sheet (ArchitecturalDecision, Constraint, Requirement, Pattern, AntiPattern, Lesson), and standard engineering practice sections (plan mode, subagent strategy, self-improvement loop targeting the graph, verification, elegance, autonomous bug fixing). README.md directory listing updated to include templates/. Intentionally scoped to workflow instructions for the consuming project — MOOSEDev's own design invariants are NOT copied into the template, keeping it lean. Rationale: consumable projects should not have to reverse-engineer the graph-first discipline from MOOSEDev's own CLAUDE.md; the template is how MOOSEDev propagates correct tool usage to the broader ecosystem of adopting projects.
docs/decisions/071-rmcp-dispatches-tool-calls-concurrently-cross-call-read-afte.md:3:Explicitly noted in tasks/todo.md as part of commit bddba142 (M1 completion): "rmcp dispatches tool calls concurrently; cross-call read-after-write relies on the client awaiting each response (true for real MCP clients). Not a concern for v1; revisit if batched/streamed calls are added." A tool call sequence such as record_important_decision immediately followed by get_relevant_context is only correct if the client awaits the first response before issuing the second — true for all LLM-driven MCP clients that serialize their tool calls. Accepted as a known limitation; not a defect in v1. Must be revisited if MOOSEDev ever adds support for batched or streamed MCP calls, which would require explicit write-before-read ordering guarantees.

# get_relevant_context topic search: search_records (BM25 over label + description) replaces search_classes (label-only)

Searching rdfs:label rather than hasTitle ensures label-only records (no hasTitle) are still found and the title text isn't double-counted. # get_relevant_context: bounded relational expansion follows record→record edges from BM25 seeds

Commit 5dc4a3ba00 (src/graph/mod.rs relevant_context() + record_neighbors()). After BM25 retrieval produces a ranked seed set, get_relevant_context performs a bounded hop-walk over outbound record→record edges (record_neighbors()) to surface lexically-distant records that are linked to the seeds but would be missed by pure keyword matching. Implementation details:

- record_neighbors(iri): enumerates all outbound quads from a project-graph subject in the project KG graph. Skips rdf:type, prov: metadata firehose, and hasRationale (its text is already inlined by build_context_item). Returns (predicate_local, neighbor_iri, neighbor_class) for neighbors that pass require_information_record — only recorded knowledge items, not arbitrary graph nodes.

- Expansion loop: seeds from the top EXPAND_FROM_TOP=3 BM25 hits; walks up to EXPAND_MAX_HOPS=2 hops; appends at most EXPAND_MAX=5 total neighbor items to the result (hard cap). Each appended item gets a "linkedVia" synthetic property showing which predicate led to it.

- Guards: skipped entirely for list-all calls (topic=None or whitespace-only) and when MOOSEDEV_EXPAND_HOPS=0 (or env var override to any other value). include_history filter applies to expanded items too.

Rationale: BM25 ranks by shared tokens — a Constraint whose title shares no tokens with the query but is linked via isMotivatedBy from a matching ArchitecturalDecision is invisible to BM25 alone. Traversal reaches it in one hop. The bounded budget (Constraint f28b0186) ensures this does not become a neighborhood dump that defeats context efficiency. The symbolic-layer principle is preserved: no LLM involvement on the expansion path.
# Relational expansion in get_relevant_context must be bounded: budgeted reach, not neighborhood dump

Commit 5dc4a3ba00 (src/graph/mod.rs, EXPAND_FROM_TOP/EXPAND_MAX_HOPS/EXPAND_MAX constants). Relational expansion in get_relevant_context is a budgeted reach to the few linked records that complete an answer — specifically the lexically-distant neighbor that BM25 alone misses — without dumping the full neighborhood. Concretely: expansion seeds from only the top-N BM25 hits (EXPAND_FROM_TOP=3), walks at most EXPAND_MAX_HOPS=2 hops outward, and appends at most EXPAND_MAX=5 total linked records. Context efficiency is the whole point of get_relevant_context: returning the entire reachable neighborhood would negate the retrieval tool's purpose of surfacing the most relevant records without overwhelming the caller's context window. Expansion is skipped entirely for list-all calls and when MOOSEDEV_EXPAND_HOPS=0.

item.text: This checkout appears to contain the recorded project memory but not the Rust source tree (`src/` is absent), so I’m grounding the answer in the newest recorded decisions about the current implementation.

Currently, `get_relevant_context(topic: ...)` uses pure symbolic BM25 retrieval via `entity_index.search_records`, searching project records over weighted text fields: `rdfs:label` at 2x and description at 1x, then ranking and taking top-k with no absolute score floor. After the BM25 seed set, it does bounded relational expansion from the top 3 hits, walking outbound record-to-record edges up to 2 hops and appending at most 5 linked records; with no topic, it instead lists instances via SPARQL.

Grounded in: “get_relevant_context topic search: search_records…”, “BM25 search_records replaces…”, and “bounded relational expansion follows record→record edges…”.
